headline: 153-run lead: Bangladesh dominate Australia on Day 2 in Darwin
summary: Tanzid Tamim scores a historic maiden Test century, helping the Tigers reach their highest-ever Test total on Australian soil.
details: Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the first Test in Darwin with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing the day at 351-6. Tanzid Tamim starred with a spectacular maiden Test century, becoming the first Bangladeshi batter to score a Test ton in Australia.

Tanzid's achievement is historic, as he is only the second Bangladeshi batter to score a century against Australia overall, after Shahriar Nafees in 2006. He also shared a 102-run second-wicket partnership with Mominul Haque.

Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto provided crucial support with a half-century, while the team's total of 351-6 is already their highest Test total in Australia, surpassing their previous record of 295 set in 2003.
The Tigers have only twice taken a first-innings lead of more than 150 runs against Australia, with the other instance occurring in 2006.

On the Australian side, Steve Smith equalled Joe Root for the most catches by a fielder in Test history with 218. Mitchell Starc also moved to 11th on the all-time list with 435 Test wickets, surpassing Kapil Dev.
Despite a late mini-collapse, Bangladesh remains in a powerhouse position as the match progresses into Day 3.

headline_marked: NCP: [[Tarique Rahman's India visit unacceptable]] without accountability for Hasina
headline: NCP: Tarique Rahman's India visit unacceptable without accountability for Hasina
summary: National Citizen Party leaders claim a visit to India would be a 'betrayal' unless New Delhi hands over Sheikh Hasina and others accused of July Uprising killings.
details: National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam called the BNP-led government 'fraudulent' and accused it of betraying the people's trust by failing to implement the referendum verdict.
Speaking at a rally in Jatrabari, Nahid Islam stated that people would not accept a visit to India by Tarique Rahman unless New Delhi is held accountable for sheltering Sheikh Hasina.
NCP spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain added that any such visit before India hands over those responsible for the July Uprising killings would be a 'betrayal of the people'.
The NCP demanded that India return those accused, including those responsible for the killings and Osman Hadi, to Bangladesh to face trial and death sentences.
Asif Mahmud also mentioned that while Sheikh Hasina and other Awami League leaders have expressed a desire to return, the NCP wants them to return specifically to face trial.
Nahid Islam further warned of movements against the government over the energy crisis, citing increased extortion, corruption, and record-breaking load-shedding.
The NCP also criticized the BNP for disregarding the July Charter by holding presidential elections under the existing provisions of Article 70.
caption:
Would a visit to India be a 'betrayal'? NCP warns Tarique Rahman's trip is unacceptable unless Hasina is handed over.

National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam called the BNP-led government 'fraudulent' and accused it of betraying the people's trust by failing to implement the referendum verdict.

Speaking at a rally in Jatrabari, Nahid Islam stated that people would not accept a visit to India by Tarique Rahman unless New Delhi is held accountable for sheltering Sheikh Hasina.

NCP spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain added that any such visit before India hands over those responsible for the July Uprising killings would be a 'betrayal of the people'.

The NCP demanded that India return those accused, including those responsible for the killings and Osman Hadi, to Bangladesh to face trial and death sentences.

Asif Mahmud also mentioned that while Sheikh Hasina and other Awami League leaders have expressed a desire to return, the NCP wants them to return specifically to face trial.

Nahid Islam further warned of movements against the government over the energy crisis, citing increased extortion, corruption, and record-breaking load-shedding.

The NCP also criticized the BNP for disregarding the July Charter by holding presidential elections under the existing provisions of Article 70.
